title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic Usage Policy update (published Oct 8, effective Nov 12) — new hardware-control, surveillance and deceptive-activity rules
bullets.summary: Adds requirements when Claude controls hardware that takes autonomous physical actions (a qualified operator must be able to observe and stop the equipment, and it must hold a safe state if Claude disconnects), bans tracking people without consent and building influence-operation tooling, and restricts entities controlled from unsupported regions.
bullets.how: Brand 9 Signs / The Construct: the CNC and vinyl-cut pipeline (ShopBot, Mimaki) driven by agents needs an operator e-stop and safe-state-on-disconnect before Nov 12. PRAGMA: add these clauses to client agent-deployment checklists, especially for high-risk (finance/legal/health) use cases.

bullets.title: DeepSeek Harness agent shell sandbox escape (CVSS 9.4, fixed in 0.1.2-alpha.1) and unpatched LMCache RCE (CVSS 9.8)
bullets.summary: OX Security disclosed a sandbox escape in DeepSeek's open-sourced Harness agent shell, fixed in 0.1.2-alpha.1; separately JFrog reported an unauthenticated RCE in LMCache (Oct 7) with, per the report, no fixed version yet.
bullets.how: The Construct: audit whether any agent shell or inference cache in the stack (Hermes workers, local model serving) uses Harness or LMCache; if so, upgrade or isolate. PRAGMA: useful talking point for client security reviews. Brand 9 Signs: no direct use.

bullets.title: Google Cloud unveils persistent Gemini agents with their own Gmail, Calendar and Drive (Gemini at Work 2026)
bullets.summary: A long-running enterprise agent orchestrates sub-agents over hours or days, each sub-agent gets its own Workspace account, and it can route work to Claude and other models.
bullets.how: The Construct: validates the persistent-agent-with-own-identity pattern we already run; study its identity/permission model. PRAGMA: competitive reference when pitching AI-operator engagements to Google Workspace shops. Brand 9 Signs: no direct use.

bullets.title: StepFun Step 5 Preview — 600B sparse MoE (27B active), 1M context, on OpenRouter; open weights slated Oct 15
bullets.summary: Priced at $1 per 1M input / $2.70 per 1M output tokens on OpenRouter, with open weights planned for October 15 (vendor claims; not independently benchmarked).
bullets.how: The Construct: candidate cheap long-context worker or second-opinion model once weights land; test before trusting. PRAGMA: possible self-host option for privacy-sensitive clients. Brand 9 Signs: no direct use.

bullets.title: Manus parent Butterfly Effect closes $500M+ round at ~$4B valuation (Oct 8)
bullets.summary: Led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital, per TechNode, signaling continued heavy investor appetite for general-purpose autonomous-agent products.
bullets.how: Market signal only: confirms demand for agent products, but nothing actionable for The Construct, Brand 9 Signs or PRAGMA beyond competitive awareness.

praxis_lesson: Agent governance is turning into a deployment gate: Anthropic's new policy requires an operator stop and safe-state for agents driving hardware, and the Harness/LMCache CVEs show agent shells are an attack surface. Build the e-stop, safe-state and sandbox-audit checks into every agent that touches a machine, before the rules or the attackers force it.
